issues.on_page: Operating Grants and Contributions 1,410,606.08, printed by function (612,178.00 / 93,750.00 / 12,911.00 / 573,677.75 / 118,089.33)
issues.issue: p2 breaks this line down by function, not into federal and state; the split comes from the fund schedules. The arithmetic holds and p4 prints Federal receipts 784,046.30, so the split is defensible, but it is not a breakdown printed for this exact line.

issues.on_page: Debt service and fees 1,508,521.13 (p2); p4 prints Redemption of principal 578,521.73, Debt service interest and fees 925,299.40, Other 4,700
issues.issue: The principal/interest split follows the fund schedules' 831 codes (pp12-14) instead of the split printed on the governmental funds statement (p4). The amounts tie (731,521.73 + 776,999.40 = 1,508,521.13) and both lines carry review, but the report itself prints a different split (a 153,000 difference).

issues.on_page: GF Instructional services 5,309,950.42 (p3) = GF instruction 5,290,396.45 (p16) + Employee Benefit 19,553.97 (p9); Support services 2,996,797.25 = GF support functions 3,460,897.25 - 464,100
issues.issue: The governmental funds statement (pp3-4) takes all 464,100 of GF-to-Depreciation/Employee Benefit transfers out of Support services and none out of instruction. The -40,000 instruction contra follows the Statement of Activities (p2) instead. decision_needed only asks about the 200,000 transportation/maintenance question, not about this second contradiction between the two statements.

Both statements count Employee Benefit Fund spending under Instruction: p3 Instructional services 5,309,950.42 = GF instruction 5,290,396.45 + 19,553.97, and p2 Instruction 5,269,950.42 = 5,290,396.45 - 40,000 + 19,553.97. Under the rules, the function the report itself uses would be 'instruction'.

issues.on_page: 3552 School Safety and Security: 739 Safety Grant 55,800.00
issues.issue: The line carries object code 739 (equipment, as in Nutrition '739 Equipment'), so it has an object and 'equipment purchases' would fit better than 'not itemized'.

issues.on_page: School Nutrition Fund, shown as a governmental fund column (p3) and in Governmental Activities (p2)
issues.issue: The extractor rules list school nutrition as an example business-type fund. This report presents it as a governmental fund, so 'governmental' follows the report and is defensible, but it departs from the rule's default (it applies to all School Nutrition lines and the top-level 'School nutrition' disbursement).
